title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out with a synthetic video call. The face and voice of a public figure were generated to open a WhatsApp conversation, and the scam then moved to ordinary channels: a supposed manager, a supposed CBI officer, and a sequence of fee demands paid through a digital payment app. The deepfake did the work of establishing authority at the start, and the rest of the scheme relied on the victim's fear of losing what he had already sent.

The failure sits at the point of contact, not inside any bank or government system. A one-to-one video call has no verification layer, so nothing in the call itself could confirm that the person on screen was who he appeared to be. Catching it would have required the victim to independently verify the offer through an official channel, or a platform-level signal that the call was synthetic. Neither is described in the reporting.

What is not established is who made the deepfake, whether the call was generated by a service or by an individual, and whether any of the people who contacted Giri after the first call were connected to its creator. A case has been registered, and a registration is not a finding of guilt.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said his manager would arrange the transfer. The manager then told Giri that Rs 5 lakh had been allotted to him and demanded fees, starting with Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

Giri paid, then a person claiming to be a CBI officer named Thakur demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Fearing he would lose his earlier money, Giri transferred more, losing over Rs 1.04 lakh in total through a digital payment app. He refused a further Rs 50,000 demand and reported the fraud to the cybercrime helpline and Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act.
